tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: The README.md file introduces FamilyWarden, a native OpenWrt parental control plugin that provides profile-based internet blocking with time schedules. It covers the project status, package structure, installation instructions, and a quick API reference. This is the best starting point before diving into the implementation.

tour.title: UCI Configuration Schema
tour.description: The UCI configuration file at /etc/config/familywarden defines the entire data model for parental control: global settings (enabled, default_policy), named profiles (devices, policy, dns_profile), and time schedules (days, start, stop). Every component in the system -- daemon, ubus API, and frontend -- reads and writes this same schema.

tour.title: Daemon Init Script and Bootstrapping
tour.description: The procd init script is the service bootstrapper for OpenWrt. It declares the familywarden service to procd, which handles start, stop, reload, and respawn. This is where the daemon gets wired into OpenWrt's boot process and how it survives router restarts.

tour.title: Shell and Ucode ubus API Plugins
tour.description: FamilyWarden exposes its control interface via OpenWrt's ubus RPC mechanism. Two implementations exist in parallel: a shell script at usr/lib/rpcd/familywarden and a ucode variant at usr/share/rpcd/ucode/familywarden. Both expose the same API (list, status, block, allow, reset, ticket, reload) used by the LuCI frontend and Home Assistant. The ACL configuration file restricts which callers can invoke each method.
tour.languageLesson: OpenWrt's ubus (micro bus) is a lightweight RPC system for inter-process communication. The rpcd plugin registers an object with methods; callers use `ubus call familywarden <method>` to invoke them. ACL files enforce that only authorized sessions (e.g., from LuCI's HTTP API) can access certain methods.

tour.title: LuCI Frontend Overview Dashboard
tour.description: The overview.js view is the main dashboard displayed when a user opens FamilyWarden in the OpenWrt web interface. It fetches profile statuses via the ubus API, renders device lists and traffic metrics, displays active schedules, and provides quick-action buttons (block/allow/ticket) for each profile. It is the highest-fan-out file in the codebase, reflecting its central role in the UI.

tour.title: LuCI Profiles and Settings Editors
tour.description: The profiles.js view handles profile creation and editing -- adding devices by MAC address, assigning schedules, and setting policies (allow/scheduled/block). The settings.js view exposes global options such as whether FamilyWarden is enabled and what the default internet policy should be. Together they form the configuration interface built on top of the ubus API from Step 4.

tour.title: LuCI Navigation and ACL Configuration
tour.description: The LuCI menu configuration file maps the four frontend views (overview, profiles, settings, info) into OpenWrt's web interface navigation tree. The accompanying ACL file grants the luci-app-familywarden package HTTP API access permissions, controlling which RPC methods the frontend can call on behalf of the browser user.

tour.title: OpenWrt Package Build Infrastructure
tour.description: Two Makefiles drive the OpenWrt package build: one for the familywarden daemon and one for luci-app-familywarden. Both follow OpenWrt's PKG_* convention (PKG_NAME, PKG_VERSION, PKG_RELEASE) and declare dependencies, sources, and build targets. Building installs the daemon, init script, ubus plugins, ACL files, and LuCI views into the correct paths on the target system.
tour.languageLesson: OpenWrt packages use a two-stage Makefile structure. The main package Makefile declares metadata and pulls sources; the OpenWrt build system (scripts/mk/openwrt.sh or the feeds system) processes it. PKG_BUILD-flags control which features or file sets are included at compile time.

tour.title: Test Infrastructure
tour.description: The test layer uses two complementary approaches: a shell-based syntax and config-generation test (basic_test.sh) that runs on the target or QEMU, and a Playwright-based end-to-end browser test (familywarden.spec.js) that exercises the full LuCI UI flow including login, profile creation, and schedule setup. The package.json declares Playwright as a devDependency for the e2e suite.
tour.languageLesson: Playwright is a browser automation framework that controls a real Chromium or Firefox instance. Tests use page.goto() to navigate, locators to find UI elements, and expect() assertions to verify behavior -- providing confidence that the entire HTTP -> ubus -> nftables chain works end-to-end.

tour.title: Implementation Planning and Architecture
tour.description: CLAUDE.md and PLAN.md together document the full scope, current status, and implementation roadmap. CLAUDE.md captures the vision (profile-based parental control with ubus API for Home Assistant integration), the UCI schema, the daemon responsibilities, and the four-phase implementation plan. PLAN.md tracks architecture decisions, bugs fixed, and test results. The plans/melodic-swimming-shamir.md file documents a proposed future migration to kernel-level nftables scheduling via procd reload triggers.
